title: A worker pool on a channel
description:
Write `public static class Workers` with:

```csharp
public static async Task<IReadOnlyList<TOut>> ProcessAsync<TIn, TOut>(
    IEnumerable<TIn> inputs, Func<TIn, Task<TOut>> work, int workers, int capacity)
```

- A bounded channel of `capacity` items carries `(index, input)` pairs from one producer to `workers` consumer tasks.
- Each consumer awaits `work(input)` and stores the result at its index, so the returned list is **in the order of the inputs**, whatever order the work finishes in.
- At most `workers` calls to `work` run at once, and they do overlap.
- If any `work` call throws, `ProcessAsync` throws that exception (after the other workers have stopped; you may let them finish their current item).
- `workers` and `capacity` must be at least 1 (`ArgumentOutOfRangeException`).
hints: Store results in an array the size of the input and write each one at its index: that keeps the order no matter which worker finishes first.
The producer must call `channel.Writer.Complete()` (or `TryComplete()`) when it has written everything, or the consumers' `await foreach` never ends. Put it in a `finally`.

For errors: a consumer that catches an exception cancels a shared `CancellationTokenSource` so the producer and the other consumers stop, then rethrows. `await Task.WhenAll(consumers)` rethrows it to the caller.
